notes: Hypothesis: always matching the anchor classifier distribution can oppose clean-teacher correction when their predicted classes differ. On source U only, multiply per-example KL(F(anchor)||F(output)) by the indicator argmax F(clean)==argmax F(anchor), then average over the full batch. Clean-teacher KL, 0.2 normalized waveform MSE and 1.5 clean anchor waveform preservation remain unchanged; no agreement threshold is fitted.

This is a frozen-classifier-guided source training method, not inference routing: both teachers are detached, source U TX truth remains hidden, and inference requires only the current packet and the two frozen experts. All-disagreement batches give a finite zero anchor term. Aggregate source U teacher-agreement counts are recorded.

Same 4096 selected source U packets, low-urban-weighted practical simulation/clean observations, seed, optimizer, 1000 updates, source-selected anchors and 5% cap as matched ungated teacher run. LoRa/WiSig frozen teacher sample forwards including smoke 12008/72032; LoRa original scipy forward uses surrogate backward.

Prior exposed source V matched comparison: teacher guidance vs no new teacher gave LoRa corrected 4/harmed 1, net +3, 95% CI -1/+7, WiSig corrected 5/harmed 3, net +2, CI -3/+8; teacher candidate failed strong-anchor half thresholds. The LoRa real-gain ancestor itself used E104 guidance and pseudo labels; WiSig R17 is F-free.

No U TX truth, source V, target IQ/truth/statistics are used in training or threshold fitting. Previously exposed source V influenced design; fixed clean/low-urban IDs, observations, controls and per-half thresholds stay unchanged. Any pass requires preregistered independent source replication before formal target testing.
